papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: The phase 3 CheckMate 227 Part 1 study (NCT02477826) demonstrated survival benefit with first-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus chemotherapy in patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Here, we report final, 7.5-year efficacy and safety results. METHODS: Adults with stage IV/recurrent NSCLC and no sensitizing EGFR/ALK mutations were stratified by programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) ≥1% (n = 1189) or <1% (n = 550) and randomized to nivolumab plus ipilimumab, nivolumab alone (PD-L1 ≥1% only), nivolumab plus chemotherapy (PD-L1 <1% only), or chemotherapy alone. Assessments included overall survival (OS), duration of response, and safety. RESULTS: At a minimum follow-up of 91.9 months, nivolumab plus ipilimumab continued to demonstrate long-term OS benefit versus chemotherapy in patients with tumor PD-L1 ≥1% (7-year OS rates, 19% versus 10%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.78; 95% CI: 0.67-0.91) or tumor PD-L1 <1% (7-year OS rates, 14% versus 4%; HR, 0.64; 95% CI: 0.51-0.79). Rates of ongoing response at 7 years were higher with nivolumab plus ipilimumab than chemotherapy among responders with tumor PD-L1 ≥1% (25% versus 3%) or tumor PD-L1 <1% (20% versus 3%). Clinical benefit with nivolumab plus ipilimumab was observed across most patient subgroups, including those with squamous or non-squamous NSCLC or selected oncogenic driver mutations. No new safety signals were observed. CONCLUSIONS: This final analysis from CheckMate 227 confirms that nivolumab plus ipilimumab confers long-term, durable clinical benefit versus chemotherapy in patients with metastatic NSCLC across both the tumor PD-L1 ≥1% and PD-L1 <1% populations, reinforcing nivolumab plus ipilimumab as a first-line treatment option for these patients.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a life-threatening complication of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). We aimed to identify predictive biomarkers associated with symptomatic CIP (sCIP) and unravel the underlying pathogenesis. METHODS: We integrated CyTOF, proteomics, single-cell RNA and V(D)J sequencing, single-cell secretomics, and spatial transcriptomics. These techniques were used to profile peripheral blood, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, and lung tissue samples from two prospective multi-center cohorts of NSCLC patients receiving ICI combination treatments. RESULTS: Elevated serum CXCL9 levels combined with high frequencies of peripheral PD-1+ CD8+ T cells after induction ICI were associated with subsequent sCIP (AUC=0.954) and inferior overall survival (HR=7.19, p=0.004). Mechanistically, PD-1+ CD8+ T cells displayed a type 1 effector profile characterized by IFN-γ and MIP-1β secretion. CXCL9/CXCR3 signaling was associated with recruitment of these cells to inflamed lung tissue. CONCLUSIONS: The CXCL9-PD-1+ CD8+ T cell axis is associated with CIP pathogenesis. This mechanism supports a potential blood-based biomarker model for CIP risk stratification and identifies a promising preventive therapeutic target to optimize clinical management.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a heterogeneous disease with no single definitive therapeutic approach. The role of neoadjuvant tyrosine kinase inhibitors in stage III ALK-positive NSCLC remains unknown. The ALNEO study evaluated the activity and safety of perioperative alectinib in this population. PATIENTS AND METHODS: ALNEO is an open-label, single-arm, multicenter phase II study enrolling treatment-naïve patients with potentially resectable stage III ALK-positive NSCLC. Patients received neoadjuvant alectinib 600 mg twice daily for 8 weeks, followed by surgery and adjuvant alectinib for up to 96 weeks. The primary end point was major pathologic response (MPR; ≤10% residual viable tumor cells) assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included pathologic complete response (pCR), objective response rate (ORR), event-free survival (EFS), disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. RESULTS: From May 2021 to July 2024, 33 patients were enrolled. The median age was 62 years (range, 33-79), 70% were female, and 52% were never smokers. Clinical stage was IIIA in 64% and IIIB in 36%. All patients completed neoadjuvant treatment, and 28 (85%) underwent surgery, most commonly lobectomy (75%). R0 resection was achieved in 24 (86%). MPR was observed in 14 patients (42%; 95% CI, 26 to 61), including four pCRs (12%; 95% CI, 3 to 28). ORR was 67%. Adjuvant treatment was initiated in 26 (79%) patients. After a median follow-up of 26.8 months, median EFS, DFS, and OS were not reached; six patients (18%) experienced disease recurrence. Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 9% and 27% of patients during neoadjuvant and adjuvant treatment, respectively. CONCLUSION: The ALNEO study met its primary end point, suggesting perioperative alectinib as a feasible and active approach in potentially resectable stage III ALK-positive NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: COPD is characterised by respiratory exacerbations, often requiring hospitalisation. Post-hospitalisation pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) can reduce risk of readmission, but very few people attend PR post exacerbation. OBJECTIVE: To compare hospital readmission rates between people with COPD who undertake a home-based PR program commenced early (≤2 weeks) after hospital discharge (ePR) with usual care. METHODS: Assessor blinded, multi-centre RCT. Participants randomised 1:1 to ePR or usual care. ePR was 8 weeks (1 physiotherapy home-visit, plus 7x weekly phone calls). The primary outcome was all-cause, non-elective hospitalisation at 12 months after rehabilitation completion. RESULTS: From Jan 2020-Jun 2024 157 participants were randomised to ePR (n=77) or usual care (n=80). The ITT analysis included 151 participants (n=73 ePR, n=78 usual care; n=6 excluded: n=5 deceased, n=1 transplant). Rate of all-cause non-elective hospitalisation was not different between groups at 12-month follow-up (ePR 60.3%, usual care 64.1%; RR 0.94 [95%CI 0.73, 1.21]). There was no difference between groups for improvements in quality of life and breathlessness at either time point. There was a clinically and statistically significant reduction in anxiety favouring ePR (10-weeks post-discharge MD -2.1 [95%CI -3.4, -0.8]; 12-months MD -1.6 [95%CI -3.0, -0.2]). ePR completion rate (≥70% sessions) was high (n=57, 74%). When compared to no rehabilitation (per protocol), ePR completers demonstrated significant improvements in breathlessness, quality of life, anxiety/depression and self-efficacy. There was one intervention-related adverse event. CONCLUSION: ePR delivered directly to patients in their homes, commenced within 2 weeks of hospital discharge, did not reduce hospital readmissions over 12 months compared to usual care but did support high program completion. When compared to no rehabilitation, improved clinical outcomes favoured ePR in those who completed the program.

papers.abstract_en: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is a rare type of lung cancer with a very poor prognosis, and its underlying molecular features remain elusive. Here, multi-omics analysis of 27 LCNEC cases along with seven small cell lung carcinomas is performed. The genomic and epigenomic alterations as well as the correlation of the genomic mutations with the pathological subtypes are characterized, which are not always consistent. Spatial omics analyses are also conducted, and most of the cases are successfully grouped into a high ASCL1 neuroendocrine (NE) subtype and high ASCL2 or YAP1 non-NE subtypes; however, an ambiguous state is observed for some specimens, which shows the simultaneous expression of NE and non-NE lineage markers. The findings of this study indicate that LCNEC may transit toward the NE or non-NE directions. By controlling the transcriptional regulatory networks of such elasticity, a new approach may be contemplated to overcome the pleiotropic therapeutic responses of LCNEC.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Obesity is associated with poor asthma outcomes. GLP-1 and dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists induce weight loss and dampen airway inflammation independent of pathways currently targeted by biologics. OBJECTIVE: To compare differences in respiratory outcomes and weight loss between GLP-1-based medications and tezepelumab in asthma patients without diabetes. METHODS: A retrospective study was performed in a multi-institutional electronic health record database. Patients with specialist-treated, obesity-associated, moderate-to-severe asthma with at least one severe exacerbation in the prior year who initiated liraglutide, semaglutide, tirzepatide, or tezepelumab between January 1, 2022 and December 31, 2025 were identified. Prevalent diabetes was excluded. Patients were followed for subsequent exacerbations, rescue inhaler prescriptions, respiratory-related healthcare encounters, and time to greater than 10% loss in body mass index. Overlap weighting accounted for imbalance in baseline asthma and obesity characteristics. RESULTS: 2779 patients were identified, of whom 133 initiated liraglutide, 1770 semaglutide, 472 tirzepatide, and 404 tezepelumab. In weighted estimates, patients starting tirzepatide experienced a lower hazard of severe exacerbation compared to tezepelumab (weighted hazard ratio [wHR] 0.41; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.24-0.70); those starting semaglutide had a similar hazard (wHR 0.99; 95% CI 0.70-1.39). Tirzepatide and semaglutide initiators attained >10% reduction in BMI sooner, had less need for rescue inhalers, and had fewer subsequent respiratory-related encounters compared to tezepelumab. CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1-based medications, and in particular dual-incretin GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists, may have comparable effectiveness to biologic therapy among patients with associated obesity without diabetes. Clinical trials are necessary to validate findings in this observational study.

papers.abstract_en: A better understanding of intratumor heterogeneity in pleural mesothelioma (PM) is crucial to implementing precision medicine for this deadly cancer. Using single-cell RNA sequencing approaches on tumor samples and derived primary cell lines, we defined four phenotypic cell types, related to overall survival in larger bulk cohorts: epithelioid, sarcomatoid, intermediate, and nondifferentiated. Some tumor samples showed intratumor phenotypic heterogeneity, associated with subclonal evolution, in which sarcomatoid cells can emerge from parental cells with an intermediate phenotype following the acquisition of copy number variations. Subclones were conserved in cell lines and retained their specific phenotypes, suggesting high phenotypic heritability. Spatial transcriptomics illustrated the link between phenotypic and subclonal evolution, showing that subclonal cells were colocalized and exhibited specific morphologies within the tumor tissue. Our study provides a comprehensive single-cell profiling of PM tumor cells and reveals a link between phenotypic evolution, clonal architecture, and tumor spatial organization.

papers.abstract_en: Small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a highly aggressive neuroendocrine malignancy characterized by rapid progression, early metastatic spread, and limited efficacy of treatment options beyond first-line chemo-immunotherapy. T-cell engagers (TCEs) have emerged as a promising immunotherapeutic strategy, redirecting cytotoxic T cells toward tumor-associated antigens independently of pre-existing antitumor immunity. Delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3), expressed in approximately 85-90% of SCLC tumors and minimally in normal tissues, represents an attractive therapeutic target. Tarlatamab, the first-in-class DLL3-directed bispecific T-cell engager, has demonstrated clinically meaningful antitumor activity in heavily pretreated patients with SCLC, including durable responses and signals of intracranial efficacy. Its safety profile reflects its mechanism of action and is primarily driven by T-cell activation and cytokine release. Treatment-emergent adverse events mainly include cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS). CRS is common but predominantly low grade (grade 1-2), with early onset and rapid resolution following supportive management, including intravenous fluids, oxygen, vasopressors, and IL-6 antagonists such as tocilizumab when clinically indicated. ICANS occurs less frequently, typically presents later, and is also mostly low grade with slower resolution. Both toxicities are generally manageable in appropriately trained clinical settings. Several additional DLL3-targeted TCEs and combination strategies are under investigation, showing encouraging preliminary efficacy and improved safety profiles. Ongoing efforts focus on optimizing outpatient administration, mitigating toxicity, and refining patient selection through biomarker development. This review summarizes the biological rationale, preclinical and clinical development, safety management, and emerging clinical evidence supporting the role of TCEs in SCLC.

papers.authors_conclusion: As evidence accumulates for the surgical curative time window, selective mediastinal lymph node management, and active surveillance of multifocal GGO, the field is shifting from simple "early detection and early treatment" toward early precise intervention; from disease-centered treatment toward whole-course patient benefit; and from survival extension toward cure. The central strategy is to exclude benign or self-limited lesions, compare the lesion's natural course with the patient's life expectancy, and integrate nodule size, solid component, lesion location, frozen-section pathology, and expected pulmonary function loss to determine surveillance interval, surgical timing, and extent of resection. Under the concept of minimally invasive surgery 3.0, treatment should shift from maximally tolerated intervention to minimum effective treatment. ... how surveillance, parenchyma-sparing surgery, selective lymph node management, and postoperative follow-up can be tailored to pursue cure while avoiding overtreatment.

papers.abstract_en: Low-dose computed tomography has increased the detection of ground-glass opacity (GGO)-featured lung cancer. Evidence from radiologic-pathologic correlation, molecular profiling, and clinical outcome studies indicates that GGO-featured lung cancer is both a distinct clinical phenotype and a special stage in the evolution of lung adenocarcinoma. Its management differs from that of conventional solid lung cancer. As evidence accumulates for the surgical curative time window, selective mediastinal lymph node management, and active surveillance of multifocal GGO, the field is shifting from simple "early detection and early treatment" toward early precise intervention; from disease-centered treatment toward whole-course patient benefit; and from survival extension toward cure. The central strategy is to exclude benign or self-limited lesions, compare the lesion's natural course with the patient's life expectancy, and integrate nodule size, solid component, lesion location, frozen-section pathology, and expected pulmonary function loss to determine surveillance interval, surgical timing, and extent of resection. Under the concept of minimally invasive surgery 3.0, treatment should shift from maximally tolerated intervention to minimum effective treatment. This expert review summarizes recent advances in personalized management of GGO-featured lung cancer and discusses how surveillance, parenchyma-sparing surgery, selective lymph node management, and postoperative follow-up can be tailored to pursue cure while avoiding overtreatment.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: This study aimed to describe the characteristics of patients admitted to internal medicine services in Spain for acute exacerbation of Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and evaluate compliance with the recommendations of GOLD and GesEPOC guidelines, including potential geographic and sex-related differences. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This is a prospective multicenter study including patients consecutively admitted between January and March 2020 for acute exacerbations to 19 Spanish hospitals. Demographic and clinical characteristics, in-hospital management, treatment at discharge, and compliance with guidelines both overall and according to geographic area and sex were analyzed. RESULTS: A total of 151 patients were included (82.8% male, mean age 75.3 ± 9.9 years, mean Charlson index 6.3 ± 2.5, and mean FEV1 48.7 ± 16.5%). The overall compliance with recommendations in the initial evaluation at admission was 42.5% for both guidelines. The overall compliance with recommendations on the treatment of exacerbations was 39.4% for GOLD and 42.5% for GesEPOC, and the overall compliance with recommendations on the treatment of stable COPD at discharge was 80.3% and 81.9%, respectively. Differences were observed in overall compliance with clinical evaluation, the use of systemic or inhaled corticosteroids for exacerbations, and the treatment of stable COPD at admission according to GesEPOC among patients from northern, central, and southern Spain. No differences in adequacy were observed based on sex. CONCLUSION: The clinical profile of patients admitted for acute exacerbation of COPD in Spain has not changed significantly in the last decade, with the exception of an increase in associated comorbidity. Compliance with the guideline recommendations is low overall (probably due to patient complexity), with some geographical variability noted with respect to specific recommendations.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate variation in endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) performance across UK services, benchmark performance against established standards and assess the feasibility of a national audit. SETTING: National clinical audit involving 28 UK hospitals. PARTICIPANTS: All consecutive EBUS procedures performed between 1 March 2024 and 30 June 2024 were eligible. 28 of 30 invited hospitals submitted data on 1859 procedures. PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: Timeliness, systematic nodal staging, lymph node adequacy, sensitivity, negative predictive value (NPV), biomarker adequacy and repeat procedure rates. RESULTS: Overall, 1859 EBUS procedures were analysed. Median age was 68 years (IQR 59–75), and 57% were male. No hospital achieved the target for >85% of diagnostic or staging procedures within 5 days of referral. Among 614 staging procedures, 80% met the criteria for systematic nodal staging, and 20% of sampled lymph nodes were inadequate. Staging sensitivity was 81%, with 7/18 (39%) services meeting the prevalence-adjusted benchmark; NPV was 86%, with 10/18 (56%) meeting the benchmark. Among 577 diagnostic EBUS procedures for suspected lung cancer, diagnostic sensitivity was 91%, although only 84% of non-small cell lung cancer cases had adequate tissue for complete biomarker testing. CONCLUSIONS: National EBUS benchmarking is feasible and demonstrates substantial variation across UK services. Important gaps were identified in timeliness, systematic staging, nodal adequacy and biomarker yield, supporting national audit to benchmark services and drive quality improvement.

papers.abstract_en: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy can produce uneven responses across the primary tumour, regional lymph nodes, and occult systemic disease. Pathology, circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA), and imaging capture different consequences of this response, so their disagreement can contain clinically relevant biological information. This structured narrative review examines same-patient evidence in resectable non-small cell lung cancer and interprets discordance through anatomical compartment, sampling time, and local immune context. Paired tissue studies show distinct primary and nodal immune ecologies and response-associated lymphoid and myeloid programmes. Spatial clonality and unequal shedding shape the circulating signal, while inflammatory and reparative tissue changes can sustain imaging abnormalities after tumour regression. These observations inform four proposed principles for multidisciplinary interpretation. Separate primary and nodal reporting preserves compartment-specific response information. Presurgical ctDNA clearance indicates molecular response, not proof of tissue eradication. Confirmed postoperative molecular conversion provides a rationale for reassessing current disease status. For imaging conflicts that could alter curative-intent management, lesion-level review can identify when tissue confirmation would be feasible and decision-changing. A postoperative pathology-molecular residual disease matrix organises research questions while preserving nodal findings, unresolved lesions, and serial molecular trajectory. The immediate contribution is to identify which additional observation can resolve a consequential conflict; treatment adaptation then requires evidence that acting on the result benefits patients. Biomarker discordance is therefore an interpretive problem with biological content, rather than a reason to let the most favourable test define the entire response.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Persistent symptoms after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) are common after hospitalization, but longitudinal changes in symptom burden and their relationship with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) remain incompletely understood. METHODS: In this prospective single-center observational study, hospitalized adults with PCR-confirmed COVID-19 were assessed during the acute phase and at 3-month follow-up. Symptom burden was operationally defined as the count of 16 predefined binary symptoms. Changes were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank and McNemar tests with false discovery rate correction. Associations between within-patient changes in symptom burden and changes in SF-36 domains were assessed using Spearman correlations with false discovery rate correction. RESULTS: Among 49 patients with complete symptom data, median symptom burden decreased from 4 (IQR 5) at baseline to 2 (IQR 3) at follow-up (Z = -3.863, p < 0.001). Symptom burden decreased in 35 patients (71.4%) and increased in 8 (16.3%). Loss of appetite, diarrhea/vomiting, dizziness, sleep disturbances, headache, and fever decreased significantly, whereas hair loss increased at follow-up. Among 48 patients with complete paired data, changes in symptom burden correlated inversely with changes in seven SF-36 domains, most strongly for vitality (ρ = -0.343), social functioning (ρ = -0.318), and emotional well-being (ρ = -0.289), but none remained significant after FDR correction. CONCLUSIONS: Symptom burden decreased within three months after COVID-19 hospitalization. Although higher symptom burden was associated with poorer HRQoL at follow-up, associations between changes in symptom burden and changes in HRQoL were not statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Accurate differentiation between malignant pleural effusion (MPE) and tuberculous pleural effusion (TPE) remains a critical clinical challenge, attributed to the suboptimal sensitivity of pleural effusion (PE) cytology for MPE and low microbiological positivity rate for TPE. This study evaluated the diagnostic value of individual and combined biomarkers derived from PE and peripheral blood (PB) to assist in the clinical differential diagnosis of MPE and TPE. METHODS: This retrospective study included 290 patients (102 MPE, 188 TPE). Clinical and laboratory data were retrieved from electronic medical records (EMRs). Diagnostic performance of 18 individual and 74 combined biomarkers was assessed via ROC curve analysis. RESULTS: MPE patients were older (median 69 vs. 53 years, p < 0.001) with more females (57% vs. 29%, p < 0.001). PE-CEA showed the best single-biomarker performance (AUC = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.91-0.98), followed by PB-CYFRA21-1 (AUC = 0.91) and PB-CEA (AUC = 0.90). Eight combined biomarkers outperformed PE-CEA; PE-SPOT/PE-CEA had the highest AUC (0.98, 95% CI: 0.96-0.99). CONCLUSION: Combined PE and PB biomarker ratios show promising preliminary diagnostic potential for MPE-TPE differentiation. PE-CEA is optimal alone, PE-SPOT/PE-CEA is the best combination. These findings could inform future validation studies of stratified diagnostic approaches.

papers.abstract_en: Multimorbidity, defined as the presence of two or more chronic conditions, represents a significant challenge in the management of COPD, a complex and highly prevalent disease. The coexistence of chronic conditions such as cardiovascular or metabolic diseases increases the frequency and severity of COPD exacerbations, complicates treatment decisions and worsens patient outcomes. These coexisting diseases may share underlying mechanisms, including systemic inflammation, oxidative stress and risk factors such as smoking, which accelerate disease progression. In this review, we discuss the prevalence and clinical significance of multimorbidity in COPD, with a focus on shared risk factors, the pathophysiological mechanisms and the impact on outcomes. Additionally, we examine current disease management strategies for COPD and multimorbidity, highlighting the need for a multidisciplinary, personalised approach, and discuss the role of biomarkers in coexisting conditions.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Serial oxygenation measurements may describe early risk in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF), but incremental prediction beyond an initial PaO₂/FiO₂ (P/F) ratio is uncertain. METHODS: We studied operationally defined AHRF in MIMIC-IV and replicated the trajectory framework in eICU-CRD. Mean P/F during 0-6 h (≥ 150 versus < 150 mmHg) and change during the second window ( ≥ + 30 versus < + 30 mmHg) defined four groups. Mortality prediction used a 12-hour landmark and a common MIMIC-IV sample, with repeated five-fold cross-validation, C-statistics, Brier scores, integrated Brier scores, and calibration. RESULTS: Among 14,322 eligible MIMIC-IV patients, 3,358 had paired early P/F measurements; 651 died within 28 days. Mortality was 11.6%, 14.9%, 23.6%, and 43.6% in groups A-D. Of 3,345 patients surviving to 12 h, 3,051 had complete comparison variables. The out-of-fold C-index was 0.624 for initial P/F, 0.647 for the 0-6-hour mean, and 0.666 for mean P/F plus change. Adding change to a model containing age, sex, vasopressor records, PEEP, and mean P/F changed the C-index from 0.703 to 0.706, with a small reduction in Brier score. In eICU-CRD, 12,141 patients had paired measurements and 12,020 had known hospital outcomes; the group mortality gradient was reproduced. CONCLUSIONS: Early P/F trajectory described mortality strata across two ICU databases. Continuous change provided modest additional predictive information, while incremental discrimination beyond clinical variables and early mean P/F remained uncertain. papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To develop a multimodal model for predicting progression-free survival (PFS) and survival probability of immunotherapy in patients with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS: This retrospective study included 182 inoperable NSCLC patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors. The primary endpoint was defined as durable clinical benefit (DCB, PFS ≥ 6 months) and non-durable clinical benefit (NDB, PFS < 6 months). Overall survival (OS) was the secondary endpoint for long-term efficacy. Clinical characteristics were selected using univariate and multivariate regression analyses. Radiomics features were extracted from pre-treatment computed tomography (CT) images, and pathomics features were extracted from whole slide images. A multimodal integrated model was constructed by combining clinical characteristics, radiomics-pathomics features, and utilizing multiple machine learning classifiers. The performance of the model was evaluated by plotting the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and calculating the area under the curves (AUC). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox regression analysis were applied to analyze OS. RESULTS: The multimodal model using Logistic regression classifier demonstrated better predictive performance in distinguishing DCB from NDB than any unimodal models (including the clinical, radiomics and pathomics model), with AUC of 0.90 (95%CI: 0.82-0.98) in the test cohort. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression analysis revealed significant survival differences between DCB and NDB groups stratified by the multimodal model. Two nomograms were developed to predict DCB and survival probabilities, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The combination of radiomics and pathomics features showed complementary value in predicting the efficacy and prognosis of immunotherapy, potentially improving individualized treatment in NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Understanding respiratory virus transmission requires integrating pathogen genomic data with detailed epidemiological context. We analyzed >85,000 SARS-CoV-2 genomes linked to epidemiological data collected in Massachusetts from November 2021 to January 2023. Collected in 666 settings, including schools, colleges, and skilled nursing facilities, this dataset enabled direct comparison of within-setting transmission to community-wide risk. Elevated transmission was concentrated in specific age-defined subpopulations-older adolescents in schools, undergraduates in colleges, and residents in nursing facilities-with little additional risk among other groups, notably including staff. Young adults, particularly in colleges, played a disproportionate role in spread, and new viral lineages consistently expanded first within this group. Viral spread followed reproducible urban-to-rural gradients, and vaccination was associated with reduced onward transmission. We further estimated sequencing thresholds required for timely detection of emerging variants. Together, these findings reveal consistent demographic and spatial structure in SARS-CoV-2 transmission that can inform viral respiratory pathogen genomic surveillance.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory Medicine, University of Patras, Patras, Greece.
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Managing patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and concomitant lung cancer is a major clinical challenge due to increased incidence and negative impact on quality of life and mortality. Evidence-based recommendations are lacking. This European Respiratory Society (ERS) clinical practice guideline provides recommendations to balance oncological benefits against treatment-associated toxicity. METHODS: An ERS multidisciplinary Task Force of experts and patient representatives produced 11 conditional recommendations across seven PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome) questions and two narrative questions; for one PICO question no recommendation was issued. Systematic reviews were performed for each question. Evidence certainty was assessed using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation) approach (for PICOs) and recommendations were formulated using the Evidence-to-Decision framework. RESULTS: For early-stage lung cancer, the Task Force suggests surgical resection in medically fit patients. Postoperative risk necessitates systematic preoperative evaluation, perioperative antifibrotic therapy discussion and protective perioperative strategies. For stereotactic radiotherapy, a conditional recommendation for either the intervention or the comparison was issued, balancing potential oncological benefit against radiation pneumonitis. In locally advanced lung cancer, the Task Force suggests not administering concurrent radio-chemotherapy, due to very high acute exacerbation rates. For advanced lung cancer, chemotherapy is suggested in medically fit patients, where survival benefits outweigh increased toxicity risks. For stage IV lung cancer, evidence for immunotherapy was limited, thus a conditional recommendation for either the intervention or the comparison was issued. Evidence for targeted therapy for lung cancer in patients with IPF was insufficient to support a recommendation. CONCLUSION: Given the poor prognosis of both conditions and treatment-associated risks, management requires multidisciplinary assessment of competing risks and patient preferences in experienced interstitial lung disease and oncology centres.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The use of veno-venous extracorporeal life support (VV-ECLS) for severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) has increased substantially worldwide. However, approaches to liberation from extracorporeal support remain poorly defined, with no standardized protocols or validated readiness criteria. RESEARCH QUESTION: What are the global practices for VV-ECLS liberation among Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) centers? Where is there variability in readiness assessment, liberation strategies, and use of standardized protocols? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We formulated a cross-sectional survey of 25 questions regarding liberation practices among ECLS providers. Questions focused on assessed parameters for readiness to liberate, determination of liberation success, and strategies to optimize it. Surveys were distributed electronically to 765 institutions globally registered with ELSO between July 1st and Aug 15th, 2022. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize responses. RESULTS: Of 765 centers contacted, 340 (44%) responded, with 209 (61%) reporting use of VV-ECLS. Most centers were adult-focused, intensivist-led programs with moderate annual volumes. Most respondents (58%) prioritized VV-ECLS liberation before liberation from mechanical ventilation. Readiness for liberation was most determined by improvement in oxygenation under lung-protective ventilation (92%) and respiratory system compliance (90%), while fewer centers used inspiratory effort indices (34%). Liberation strategies were heterogeneous, with progressive reduction of sweep gas flow being most common (40%). Liberation trial duration varied widely (median 120 minutes; mean 497 ± 635 minutes), and most centers performed one trial per day. Arterial blood gas abnormalities (90%) and clinical signs of respiratory distress were the primary indicators of liberation failure. Only 42% of centers reported using a formal liberation protocol. INTERPRETATION: VV-ECLS liberation practices vary substantially across centers and are largely guided by institutional experience rather than standardized evidence. These findings highlight the need for validated physiologic predictors and protocolized strategies to optimize safe and timely liberation from VV-ECLS.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Dysfunctional breathing is increasingly recognised among individuals with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC), yet data on long-term prevalence and predictors are scarce. This study assessed the prevalence of symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing, as indicated by elevated Nijmegen questionnaire (NQ) scores, four years after COVID-19 illness in adults with PCC and identified associated factors and baseline predictors by comparing individuals with and without elevated NQ scores. METHOD: In this prospective observational study, adults with PCC, both previously hospitalised and non-hospitalised for COVID-19, were recruited from a specialised post-COVID outpatient clinic. Baseline assessments (2020-2022) were analysed together with data from a digital follow-up survey in 2024. Symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing was defined as a NQ score ≥ 23 at follow-up. Between group differences were examined, and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify associated factors and baseline predictors. RESULTS: Among 288 participants (median follow-up 50 months), 143 (50%) had symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing. These individuals were younger, often female, and more frequently non-hospitalised during acute COVID-19. Baseline predictors included non-hospitalisation, higher dyspnoea severity, lower FEV1, and younger age. At four years, elevated NQ scores (≥ 23) were independently associated with higher dyspnoea severity, greater PCC-symptom burden, depressive symptoms and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome. Individuals with symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing performed worse in the six-minute walk test, one-minute sit to stand test, and maximal inspiratory pressure test at baseline, whereas lung function did not differ. Patient-reported outcomes were consistently worse compared with those with NQ scores < 23 and improved less over time. CONCLUSION: Half of the individuals with PCC in this cohort reported symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing four years after COVID-19, as indicated by a NQ score ≥ 23. Elevated NQ scores were associated with greater PCC-symptom burden and poorer health outcomes, highlighting their potential clinical relevance in long-term PCC. Future studies should combine patient-reported measures with objective assessment of breathing pattern and ventilatory function.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-positive idiopathic interstitial pneumonia (ANCA-IIP) is an interstitial lung disease (ILD) phenotype with ANCA seropositivity but no systemic evidence of vasculitis, and its disease position and treatment strategy remain uncertain. Patients with non-usual interstitial pneumonia (non-UIP) ANCA-IIP are frequently treated with glucocorticoids and immunosuppressive agents in clinical practice. However, previous studies have mainly focused on clinical characteristics and prognosis, while longitudinal changes in pulmonary function under real-world treatment conditions remain insufficiently described. This study aimed to address the following research question: among patients with ANCA-positive interstitial lung disease (ANCA-ILD), how do pulmonary function trajectories in patients with non-UIP ANCA-IIP differ from those in patients with microscopic polyangiitis-associated interstitial lung disease (MPA-ILD)? METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study screened 1,024 patients with ILD and available ANCA testing between January 2012 and January 2022. Patients with non-UIP ANCA-IIP and MPA-ILD were included according to final multidisciplinary diagnosis and high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) pattern. Locally weighted scatterplot smoothing with bootstrap 95% CIs was used to visualize 36-month trajectories of forced expiratory volume in 1 s, forced vital capacity (FVC), total lung capacity, diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLCO), and prednisone-equivalent dose. Segmented linear mixed-effects models with a 12-month knot compared pulmonary function slopes during 0 to 12 months and 12 to 36 months. RESULTS: Seventy-five patients were included: 39 with non-UIP ANCA-IIP and 36 with MPA-ILD. Compared with MPA-ILD, non-UIP ANCA-IIP showed lower inflammatory activity and no systemic involvement. Baseline DLCO was lower in MPA-ILD (53.50% vs. 65.90%; p = 0.034). During 0 to 12 months, FVC increased in non-UIP ANCA-IIP by 8.12% per 12 months, with a greater improvement than in MPA-ILD (slope difference, 8.38%/12 months; p = 0.038). During 12 to 36 months, the FVC slope was more negative in non-UIP ANCA-IIP than in MPA-ILD (slope difference, - 5.94%/12 months; p = 0.046). All-cause mortality was similar. CONCLUSION: Non-UIP ANCA-IIP showed early FVC improvement followed by later decline under real-world treatment, supporting HRCT-based phenotyping and continued pulmonary function monitoring.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Since the introduction of cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator modulators (CFTRm), more females with cystic fibrosis (CF) are becoming pregnant. Prior to the CFTRm era, pregnancy was associated with increased pulmonary exacerbations and decline in lung function. We hypothesize that in the CFTRm era, pregnant and non-pregnant females with CF would have similar rates of pulmonary exacerbations rates and lung function trajectories. METHODS: We analyzed data from the CF Foundation Patient Registry (CFFPR) (2012-2022) to evaluate females ages 18-50 years who had ever experienced a pregnancy versus those who had never been pregnant. We assessed pulmonary exacerbation events and changes in percent predicted forced expiratory volume in 1 second (ppFEV1) over time by conducting longitudinal regression models using the generalized estimating equation method after adjusting for key covariates. RESULTS: Among 5609 eligible females, 3402 (61%) had never been pregnant and 2207 (39%) had at least one pregnancy. Elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) use was more common among pregnant than non-pregnant females (72%vs. 59%; p < 0.0001). The adjusted annual pulmonary exacerbation rate did not differ between groups [adjusted rate ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.97-1.08; p = 0.35]. Pregnant females had higher ppFEV1 at all time points but the rate of change over time was similar between groups (interaction p = 0.55). CONCLUSIONS: In the CFTRm era, pregnancy was not associated with increased pulmonary exacerbation rates or accelerated decline in ppFEV1. These findings provide reassuring evidence to support counseling of females with CF who are considering pregnancy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ensifentrine improves lung function, dyspnea, and exacerbation outcomes in phase III COPD studies, but patients receiving background LAMA/LABA or LABA/LAMA/ICS therapy were excluded. Comparative effectiveness after addition to established single-inhaler triple therapy is uncertain. RESEARCH QUESTION: Among adults with COPD already receiving F/UMEC/VI or BGF, is ensifentrine initiation associated with lower 180-day exacerbation risk and improved clinical outcomes compared with continuation of the same triple inhaler? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: . We conducted parallel retrospective propensity-matched cohort studies using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adults aged ≥40 years with established COPD receiving F/UMEC/VI or BGF were classified as ensifentrine initiators or same-inhaler comparators. Baseline covariates were measured during days -365 to -1 and matched 1:1 across 45 prespecified characteristics. The primary outcome was coded COPD exacerbation (ICD-10-CM J44.1) during days 1-180. Sensitivity analyses evaluated days 31-180 and a January 2025-March 2026 calendar-restricted cohort with de novo matching. RESULTS: For F/UMEC/VI, 313 ensifentrine initiators and 4,015 comparators entered matching, yielding 304 patients per cohort. Exacerbations occurred in 39.8% versus 33.6% (RR, 1.186; 95% CI, 0.961-1.464). For BGF, 182 initiators and 851 comparators yielded 172 patients per cohort; exacerbations occurred in 40.1% versus 39.0% (RR, 1.030; 95% CI, 0.793-1.338). Hospitalization, ED utilization, and systemic glucocorticoid exposure were not significantly different in either primary analysis. Exacerbation estimates remained close to the null in lagged and calendar-restricted analyses. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults already receiving F/UMEC/VI or BGF, ensifentrine initiation was not associated with lower 180-day coded exacerbation risk or a consistent improvement in major healthcare-utilization outcomes. The concordant primary and sensitivity analyses provide early comparative-effectiveness evidence in a triple-therapy population underrepresented in pivotal ensifentrine trials.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To elucidate possible neural and molecular pathway mechanisms underlying the suppression of aerobic exercise in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) invasion. METHODS: Sympathetic nerve distribution was visualized via immunofluorescent staining in human tissue microarrays (TMAs) and mouse lung specimens. Pseudorabies virus (PRV) retrograde tracing method was employed to identify the brain-lung neural circuit, and superior cervical ganglionectomy was administrated to achieve pulmonary sympathetic denervation. Voluntary wheel running (VWR) worked as an aerobic exercise to intervene the brain-lung neural circuit to suppress mouse LUAD invasion. Norepinephrine (NE) levels and the expression of ADRB2 and MMP2 were assessed using ELISA, Western blot and qRT-PCR methods. RNA sequencing, along with transwell and wound-healing assays, were conducted on lentiviral-mediated ADRB2-overexpressing LUAD cells to evaluate migratory and invasive behaviors. RESULTS: Substantial sympathetic nerve infiltration was detected in both human and mouse LUAD specimens, with a negative correlation observed between intratumoral sympathetic nerve density and tumor volume. Retrograde tracing revealed that pulmonary sympathetic nerves are predominantly innervated by the superior cervical ganglion (SCG). SCG resection abrogated the exercise-induced elevation in intratumoral NE and reversed the anti-invasion benefits of exercise. In vitro, NE treatment downregulated MMP2 expression and impaired the migration and invasion of LUAD cells. Similarly, ADRB2 overexpression suppresses LUAD invasion by inhibiting MMP2 expression. CONCLUSION: The SCG acts as a relay hub connecting higher brain centers to intratumoral sympathetic activity, and VWR engages this SCG-mediated pathway to exert an anti-invasive effect on LUAD invasion. VWR stimulates NE release from intratumoral sympathetic nerves in LUAD. NE inhibits LUAD invasion via the ADRB2-MMP2 signaling pathway.

papers.authors: Nathan SD, Maher TM, Assassi S, Lievens D, Stowasser S, Gu H, Scholand MB
papers.affiliation_highlight: Inova Advanced Lung Disease and Transplant Program, 3300 Gallows Road, Falls Church, VA, 22046, USA.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: In the FIBRONEER-ILD trial in patients with progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF), nerandomilast reduced decline in forced vital capacity (FVC) versus placebo, with benefits on clinical outcomes and favorable safety and tolerability. We present the effects of nerandomilast in US patients. METHODS: Patients were randomized to receive nerandomilast 9 mg bid, nerandomilast 18 mg bid, or placebo, stratified by nintedanib use and HRCT pattern. In the US subgroup, we assessed change in FVC (mL) at week 52; time-to-event endpoints over the whole trial; and adverse events over the whole trial. RESULTS: Of 1176 patients, 139 (11.8%) were from the US. In the US patients, adjusted mean (SE) changes in FVC (mL) at week 52 were - 160.4 (35.7) with placebo, - 115.2 (38.6) with nerandomilast 9 mg bid (difference vs. placebo 45.2 [95% CI: -57.8, 148.2]), and - 53.4 (37.3) with nerandomilast 18 mg bid (difference vs. placebo 107.0 [95% CI: 6.2, 207.9]). The hazard ratios (95% CI) for time to first acute exacerbation of ILD, hospitalization for respiratory cause, or death were 0.88 (0.42, 1.81) for nerandomilast 9 mg bid and 0.52 (0.23, 1.18) for nerandomilast 18 mg bid versus placebo. Adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 14.0, 11.4 and 8.9% of the placebo, nerandomilast 9 mg bid and nerandomilast 18 mg bid groups, respectively. CONCLUSION: In the FIBRONEER-ILD trial, the effects of nerandomilast in US patients were consistent with the overall population, with a reduction in FVC decline, numerically reduced risk of adverse clinical outcomes, and favorable safety and tolerability.

However, direct transport to hospital-based settings is not supported without local recalibration because of pronounced spectrum bias.
papers.ai_note: 结局为自报医生诊断CLD，存在测量偏倚风险；主要结局为横断面患病率识别而非未来发病预测，临床外推有限；中国临床队列AUROC降至0.693且校准O/E=2.763，提示模型在非社区人群严重失准，作者亦承认；模型判别力中等（AUROC~0.77），未报告与现有筛查工具的增量比较；信息不足：未报告决策曲线分析具体数值、未报告各队列患病率差异
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic lung disease (CLD) is an important cause of morbidity among postmenopausal women, yet simple non-invasive community screening tools are lacking. We aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable multivariable prediction model for identifying prevalent self-reported physician-diagnosed CLD in this population. METHODS: We analyzed postmenopausal women from the US Health and Retirement Study (HRS; development n = 4,578, internal validation n = 1,962), with external validation in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA; n = 4,574) and a Chinese clinical cohort (n = 650). The primary outcome was prevalent self-reported or clinically recorded physician-diagnosed CLD, including chronic bronchitis, emphysema, or COPD where available. Predictors were selected via nested LASSO penalization. Twelve candidate statistical and machine-learning algorithms were benchmarked; the primary multivariable logistic regression model was evaluated on native uncalibrated probabilities at a locked screening threshold (9.81%) across discrimination, calibration, and clinical net benefit. RESULTS: The current 9-predictor model retained smoking status, self-rated health, arthritis, heart disease, osteoporosis, basic activities of daily living difficulty, depressive symptoms, physical activity, and employment. The multivariable logistic regression model achieved AUROCs of 0.771 (95% CI, 0.748-0.793) in HRS development, 0.769 (0.734-0.803) in internal validation, 0.762 (0.735-0.790) in ELSA external validation, and 0.693 (0.634-0.750) in the Chinese cohort. Current smoking and poor self-rated health showed the strongest associations with prevalent CLD. In the Chinese clinical cohort, the model exhibited severe calibration underestimation (observed-to-expected ratio 2.763), demonstrating negative external validation driven by spectrum bias between community and hospital-based settings. CONCLUSION: A parsimonious 9-predictor logistic regression model achieves acceptable discrimination and calibration across community cohorts for identifying prevalent self-reported physician-diagnosed CLD among community-dwelling postmenopausal women. However, direct transport to hospital-based settings is not supported without local recalibration because of pronounced spectrum bias.

papers.title_zh: Real-world outcomes of mediastinoscopic esophagectomy for esophageal cancer: a propensity score-matched analysis.
papers.title_en: Real-world outcomes of mediastinoscopic esophagectomy for esophageal cancer: a propensity score-matched analysis.
papers.authors: Sasaki K, Noda M, Tsuruda Y, Shimonosono M, Okubo K, Baba K, Arigami T, Ohtsuka T et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Digestive Surgery, Graduate School of Medical and Dental Sciences, Kagoshima University, 8-35-1 Sakuragaok…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Mediastinoscopic esophagectomy (ME) has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to thoracoscopic esophagectomy (TE), particularly for patients with high surgical risk. However, the indications for ME are heterogeneous, and direct comparisons with TE in clinical settings remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the perioperative and oncological outcomes of ME in selected patients using propensity score matching. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 260 patients who underwent esophagectomy for esophageal cancer, of whom 187 patients who underwent either TE or ME were included in the analysis. At our institution, ME was preferentially selected for patients with advanced age, impaired pulmonary function, comorbidities, or prior thoracic disease, whereas bulky tumors or clinically evident mediastinal lymph node metastases were generally excluded. After propensity score matching using 7 clinically relevant preoperative variables, 34 patients were included in each group. Perioperative outcomes, survival, recurrence patterns, and causes of death were analyzed. RESULTS: Overall morbidity, including pneumonia and recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy, did not significantly differ between the TE and ME groups. The number of dissected lymph nodes was significantly lower in the ME group (P < 0.001). With a median follow-up period of > 50 months, no significant differences were observed in overall survival (OS), relapse-free survival (RFS), or disease-specific survival (DSS). Although OS tended to be longer in the TE group, DSS was comparable between the groups. No apparent increase in locoregional recurrence was observed in the ME group, despite the reduced extent of mediastinal lymphadenectomy. Non-esophageal cancer-related mortality was significantly higher in the ME group (P < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: ME may be a feasible surgical option for selected high-risk patients, with acceptable disease-specific and locoregional control. However, the present findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the retrospective design, limited sample size, heterogeneous indications for ME, and potential residual selection bias.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: In the placebo-controlled FIBRONEER-IPF trial in patients with IPF, nerandomilast reduced decline in forced vital capacity (FVC), with benefits on clinical outcomes and favorable safety and tolerability. We evaluated the effects of nerandomilast in the US patients. METHODS: Patients were randomized to receive nerandomilast 9 mg bid, nerandomilast 18 mg bid, or placebo, stratified by antifibrotic therapy (nintedanib/pirfenidone versus neither). In the US subgroup, we assessed change in FVC at week 52; time-to-event endpoints over the whole trial; adverse events over the whole trial. RESULTS: Of 1177 patients, 196 (16.7%) were from the US. In US patients, adjusted mean (SE) changes in FVC (mL) were - 257.9 (33.6) with placebo, - 152.7 (32.9) with nerandomilast 9 mg bid (difference vs. placebo 105.2 [95% CI 13.0, 197.4]), and - 126.2 (36.9) with nerandomilast 18 mg bid (difference vs. placebo 131.7 [95% CI 33.8, 229.6]. Compared with placebo, the hazard ratios for time to first acute exacerbation of IPF, hospitalization for respiratory cause, or death were 0.91 (95% CI 0.49, 1.67) for nerandomilast 9 mg bid and 0.60 (95% CI 0.30, 1.22) for nerandomilast 18 mg bid. CONCLUSION: The effects of nerandomilast 18 mg bid in US patients in the FIBRONEER-IPF trial were consistent with the overall population. Nerandomilast 18 mg bid slowed FVC decline, with numerical reductions in the risk of clinical outcomes, and favorable safety and tolerability.

papers.authors: Köhler D, Biedritzky A, Burkard P, Liang C, Tang L, Bernard A, Dignus P, Steiner T et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Anesthesiology and Intensive Care Medicine, University Hospital, Tübingen, Tübingen, Germany.
papers.authors_conclusion: Together, our study shows that GPIb is a central mediator of neutrophil migration into the alveolar space and the defense mechanisms against the external invasion of pathogens.
papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要全文未给出任何样本量、效应量、CI或P值，小鼠肺泡中性粒细胞浸润、血小板-中性粒细胞复合物、NET形成、Klebsiella肺炎生存率与细菌载量，以及ARDS患者死亡率关联均仅有定性方向描述，无法评估效应大小与统计学可靠性；患者生物样本分析为观察性关联，不能推断因果或指导临床干预；作者结论以central mediator定性表述，超出所呈现数据（无定量、无机制挽救实验）可支撑的强度；GPIb阻断在减轻ALI的同时降低抗感染防御（生存率下降、细菌载量升高），该治疗窗权衡未被进一步量化。
papers.abstract_en: The acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a life-threatening, inflammatory disease state of the lung. Self-propagating inflammation within the alveolar space and excessive infiltration of neutrophils into the pulmonary airspace are the main mechanisms underlying the dysfunction. A role of platelets in the pathogenesis of ARDS is suggested, but the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. We hypothesized that platelet glycoprotein (GP)Ib is an important contributor of platelet activation in this context. To highlight the contribution of the GPIb to the acute phase of experimental ALI in mice, we exposed mice genetically lacking functional GPIb (GPIb-IL-4tg) and wild-type (WT) mice injected with a function blocking anti-GPIb antibody to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) inhalation. GPIb-IL-4tg mice as well as anti-GPIb-treated mice displayed reduced neutrophil infiltration of the alveolar space in response to LPS. GPIb-IL-4tg mice as well as anti-GPIb-treated WT mice showed reduced interactions of platelets with neutrophils in comparison to controls, resulting in reduced platelet-neutrophil complexes and mitigated formation of neutrophil extracellular traps. Since these mechanisms are important for defense against external invasion of pathogens, we exposed GPIb-IL-4tg mice to Klebsiella pneumoniae and found reduced survival with increased bacterial load in these animals. Last, translational evaluation of biosamples of patients with ARDS showed that patients with low plasma levels of the shed GPIbα ectodomain (glycocalicin) exhibited higher mortality and worsened overall outcome. Together, our study shows that GPIb is a central mediator of neutrophil migration into the alveolar space and the defense mechanisms against the external invasion of pathogens.

papers.authors: Yuan M, West BR, Foreman WB, Powers C, Feng Z, Taylor AL, Yu X, Wang G et al.

papers.abstract_en: Extensive mutations in SARS-CoV-2 spike protein have rendered most therapeutic monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) ineffective. However, here we describe how VYD222 (pemivibart), a human mAb re-engineered from ADG20 (adintrevimab) exhibits substantially improved neutralization potency and breadth against SARS-CoV-2 variants despite substantial virus evolution. VYD222 received FDA Emergency Use Authorization for pre-exposure prophylaxis of COVID-19 in certain immunocompromised adults and adolescents. Here we show potent neutralization of this antibody against a broad range of emerging variants, including the recently dominant XFG. X-ray crystal structures of VYD222 in complex with the receptor-binding domains of prototype SARS-CoV-2 and Omicron BA.5 demonstrate the molecular basis of how VYD222 accommodates the mutations in SARS-CoV-2 variants that escape other previous FDA-approved antibodies. Notably, many of the mutations between ADG20 and VYD222 occur in the second shell outside the paratope contact residues. Deep mutational scanning indicates that SARS-CoV-2's ability to escape VYD222 is constrained by structural compatibility and the need to maintain receptor binding. These findings provide crucial insights into the escape-resistant neutralization of VYD222 against a broad panel of clinically relevant SARS-CoV-2 variants and offer valuable guidance for risk assessment of emergent variants.

papers.authors: Grau M, Pagès-Fernández C, Vilaplana-Carnerero C, Toledo D, Díaz N, Llonch-Diaz C, Marquínez Noriega S, Fernández-Villa T et al.

No significant associations were observed with length of hospital stay or short-term post-discharge outcomes. Early recognition and hospital referral remain important components of CAP management.
papers.ai_note: 唯一达到统计学显著的ICU转入终点其95%CI下限仅1.02，恰位于边界，易受多重比较与残余混响影响；调整模型仅纳入社会人口学、生活方式、季节、疫苗接种与合并症，未见肺炎严重程度指标（如CURB-65/PSI）校正，延迟入院与ICU转入的关联可能由入院时病情严重度混杂所致；30天复合终点HR 0.87方向上偏向延迟组有利但CI跨越1，摘要未讨论；研究限于15–64岁人群，结论外推至老年CAP患者信息不足
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Evidence on the association between delayed hospital admission and the clinical course of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is limited. The objective was to assess the association between delayed hospital admission and intensive care unit (ICU) admission, length of stay and a composite outcome of 30-day readmission or death in adults hospitalised with CAP. METHODS: Multicentre observational cohort study across 16 hospitals in eight Spanish autonomous communities. Individuals aged 15–64 years hospitalised with CAP were followed during hospitalisation and up to 30 days after discharge. Delayed hospital admission was defined as admission occurring ≥7 days after symptom onset. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the association with ICU admission, generalised linear models with Gamma distribution to evaluate length of stay and Cox proportional hazards models to analyse the composite 30-day outcome, adjusting for sociodemographic and lifestyle-related factors, season, vaccination status and comorbidities. RESULTS: A total of 809 patients were included, of whom 294 (36.3%) were admitted ≥7 days after symptom onset. Delayed admission was associated with a higher risk of ICU admission (adjusted OR 1.77, 95% CI 1.02 to 3.08), but it was not associated with longer hospital stay (adjusted mean ratio 1.09, 95% CI 0.92 to 1.29) or with 30-day readmission or death (adjusted HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.47 to 1.61). CONCLUSION: Delayed hospital admission for CAP is associated with a higher likelihood of ICU admission. No significant associations were observed with length of hospital stay or short-term post-discharge outcomes. Early recognition and hospital referral remain important components of CAP management.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECT: The purpose of this study was to compile the traits of individuals who tested positive for T. whipplei through targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS), thereby improving awareness and comprehension of this rare pathogen. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on individuals with T. whipplei identified in 848 BALF samples, detected by tNGS from 21 September 2022 to 1 March 2024 at The First Hospital of Changsha. Data regarding clinical features, laboratory data, and CT images were gathered for evaluation. RESULTS: Forty-three BALF samples from forty-four (44/848, 5.2%) patients were positive for T. whipplei (one patient was excluded due to incomplete data). Twenty-eight patients were male with an average age of 46.9 years. The main symptoms included cough(38/43), expectoration(34/43), dyspnea(15/43),fever(14/43), hemoptysis/bloody sputum(5/43), myalgia(4/43), fatigue(2/43), vomiting(3/43), abdominal pain (2/43), and headache (2/43). Chronic liver disease (including fatty liver, chronic hepatitis C and chronic hepatitis B) was the most common comorbidity (n = 13, 30.2%), followed by chronic lung disease (n = 8, 18.6%). The levels of erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) were significantly higher in the pneumonia group compared to the non-pneumonia group. Conversely, the ages were significantly lower in the pneumonia group (P < 0.05). T. whipplei was the exclusive pathogen in 6 samples, while Epstein-Barr virus was the most frequently detected pathogen, followed by Haemophilus influenzae. The most prevalent finding on chest CT scans was lung nodules (18/43, 41.9%), which included fourteen solid nodules and five ground-glass nodules (three cases of calcified nodules attributed to pulmonary tuberculosis were excluded). CONCLUSION: In conclusion, our study suggests that T. whipplei may play a pathogenic role in various pulmonary diseases, warranting clinical attention during routine clinical practice. The application of tNGS technology can effectively improve the detection rate of rare pathogens, potentially providing references for clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND & AIM: Robust evidence to inform the use of parenteral prostacyclin agents (PPAs) in adults with congenital heart disease-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension (CHD-PAH) is lacking. We aimed to evaluate long-term haemodynamic, functional, and survival outcomes in a contemporary single-centre cohort of patients with CHD-PAH treated with PPA. METHOD: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adults with CHD-PAH treated with parenteral prostacyclin therapy at a single tertiary centre from 2000 to 2024. RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients initiated a PPA between 2000 and 2024 (epoprostenol, n=17, intravenous treprostinil, n=7, subcutaneous treprostinil, n=5). Median age at initiation was 36 years, and two-thirds had unrepaired congenital lesions. At first follow-up, right heart catheterisation after starting PPA therapy, prostacyclin therapy was associated with significant reductions in mean pulmonary artery pressure (-7.7 mmHg; p=0.003) and pulmonary vascular resistance (-5.4 Wood Units; p=0.001), as well as increases in cardiac index (1.2 L/min/min2; p=0.002), and pulmonary artery oxygen saturation (9%; p=0.005). Haemodynamic improvements were similar between patients receiving epoprostenol and those receiving treprostinil. Five- and 10-year survival rates were 86% and 58%, respectively, and three patients were able to undergo delayed defect closure. CONCLUSIONS: In adults with CHD-PAH, parenteral prostacyclin therapy is associated with significant improvements in pulmonary haemodynamics and functional capacity, along with favourable long-term survival. These findings highlight the need for larger multicentre studies to refine patient selection and optimise treatment strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Neoadjuvant or perioperative chemoimmunotherapy has become a standard treatment option for selected patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), with eligibility determined by tumor stage, nodal involvement, oncogenic-driver status, regimen, and jurisdiction. Even so, most patients do not achieve a pathological complete response, and the determinants of resistance in early-stage disease remain incompletely understood. Tumor-associated macrophages are a key, and targetable, component of that resistance. We argue that abundance alone is an insufficient predictor of whether the myeloid compartment supports or suppresses a checkpoint-dependent response, and that macrophage state, namely the dominant subset, its spatial niche, and its trajectory under therapy, adds explanatory and therapeutic information whose weight remains to be established. Single-cell and spatial studies have identified metabolically distinct SPP1+, CCL18+, and oncofetal STAB1+ states associated with immunosuppressive niches in NSCLC, although these labels vary between datasets and their functional assignments are provisional. Limited serial neoadjuvant data from a single cohort suggest that treatment expands tissue-resident macrophages and shifts tumor-associated macrophages toward a neutral rather than antitumor phenotype, most evidently in tumors that reached a major pathological response. Current agents, including CSF1R and CD47-SIRPα blockade, TREM2, LILRB2 and PI3Kγ inhibitors, and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) macrophages, act on programs that cut across these subsets rather than on the subsets themselves, and almost all efficacy evidence derives from advanced or preclinical disease. The resectable, biomarker-rich perioperative window is nonetheless the most informative setting in which to test subset-informed myeloid reprogramming.

papers.abstract_en: Pleural mesothelioma is a rare, asbestos-related malignancy with limited therapeutic options and dismal survival. Despite regulatory efforts, ongoing exposures, long disease latency and cases without recognized exposure suggest that pleural mesothelioma will remain a global challenge for decades. Immune checkpoint inhibitors yield modest, although clinically meaningful benefit in a subset of patients, and histology alone incompletely captures the pronounced intra- and inter-patient heterogeneity that drives prognosis and treatment responses. Multi-omic studies depict pleural mesothelioma as a tumor suppressor loss malignancy with low mutation rates, extensive structural genomic damage and a spectrum of immune states. In this review, we bridge genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic and immune-profiling data to explain how asbestos-induced genomic fragility, germline predisposition and the tumor immune microenvironment interact to shape disease biology and therapeutic vulnerability. We highlight how histo-molecular and immune-vascular continua refine risk stratification beyond histology, and how recurrent alterations intersect with immune infiltration, checkpoint expression and T cell dysfunction to potentially modulate immune checkpoint inhibitors sensitivity. These insights support comprehensive and integrative profiling to develop robust biomarkers, optimize patient selection and guide rational combinatorial strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is a leading cause of death in the US and worldwide, with females and Black individuals disproportionately affected. We explore possible biological mechanisms for this disparity using data from the COPDGene Study. We analyzed clinical, demographic, social determinants of health (SDoH), and omics data from 1,079 current and former smokers. To quantify socio-environmental risk, we constructed a novel "vulnerability score" combining 10 SDoH metrics. Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) identified correlated gene and proteomic signatures, which were associated with social vulnerability via linear mixed models. High-dimensional mediation analysis evaluated whether these SDoH-associated molecular signatures mediate disparities across race, sex, and COPD outcomes. We used the heterogeneity in integration and prediction (HIP) method to further identify possible race/sex-specific biomarkers of COPD outcomes. Vulnerability score was associated with COPD outcomes including exacerbation frequency and dyspnea. Twenty-two proteins were significantly associated with vulnerability score after false discovery rate adjustment (adjusted p < 0.05). Among these, mediation analysis identified six proteins-sRAGE, DC-SIGN, Selenoprotein W, IgD, Beta-Ala-His dipeptidase, and PTP-1C-that significantly mediated the relationship between race and COPD outcomes. HIP analysis identified 22 of 70 candidate proteins with distinct race- or sex-specific functional effects in COPD. The implementation of vulnerability score demonstrates that social environmental context correlates with biological heterogeneity in COPD. By identifying SDoH-associated proteomic signatures mediating sex- and race-associated differences, our study provides plausible social-environmental biological pathways through which disparities in COPD outcomes manifest. These insights can inform personalized respiratory medicine and guide public health interventions to mitigate health disparities.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To identify clinical factors associated with infection rather than colonization of pulmonary infection,when Enterococcus faecium is detected by mNGS in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. METHODS: Clinical data were retrospectively analyzed from 64 ICU patients admitted to Changsha First Hospital between March 2025 and March 2026 in whom E. faecium was detected in BALF by mNGS. According to integrated clinical diagnosis and etiological assessment, patients were categorized into an infection group (n = 32) and a colonization group (n = 32). Baseline characteristics, invasive procedures, resistance profiles, and in-hospital outcomes were compared between groups. Factors associated with E. faecium pneumonia were identified using binary logistic regression. RESULTS: Age, sex, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, cerebrovascular disease, chronic liver disease, chronic kidney disease, inherited metabolic disease, history of abdominal surgery, malnutrition, consciousness status, indwelling gastric tube, tracheal intubation/tracheostomy, prolonged hospitalization with broad-spectrum antibiotic exposure, hospital stay ≥6 days, and in-hospital outcomes did not differ significantly between the two groups (all p > 0.05). In univariate analysis, dysphagia, concomitant viral infection, indwelling urinary catheterization, and central venous catheterization were more frequent in the infection group, whereas coronary heart disease, underlying pulmonary disease, and glucocorticoid use were more frequent in the colonization group (all p < 0.05). Exploratory multivariable analysis identified concomitant viral infection, indwelling urinary catheterization, and central venous catheterization as factors associated with infection rather than colonization of pulmonary infection (all p < 0.05). According to the mNGS reports, resistance genes were detected in 8 patients (25.0%) in the infection group, including vanM + vanA in 3 patients, vanA in 1 patient, and vanM in 4 patients. In the colonization group, resistance genes were detected in 4 patients (12.5%), all of whom carried vanM + vanA. These genes are primarily associated with glycopeptide resistance. CONCLUSION: Concomitant viral infection, indwelling urinary catheterization, and central venous catheterization may be important clinical clues for interpreting the significance of BALF mNGS-detected E. faecium. When E. faecium is detected in BALF by mNGS, its etiological significance should be determined by integrating clinical manifestations, risk factors, imaging findings, and conventional microbiological evidence. Antimicrobial therapy should be individualized according to resistance gene detection, phenotypic susceptibility testing, infection site, and patient-specific organ function.

papers.abstract_en: The advancement of RNA therapeutics, particularly small interfering RNA (siRNA), offers promising new approaches for the treatment of pulmonary diseases driven by aberrant gene expression and chronic inflammation like asthma and COPD. In this study, we systematically engineered dry powder inhaler (DPI) formulations containing low (0.8%) and high (2%) siRNA-loaded lipid nanoparticle (LNP) concentrations using spray drying. The matrix-forming excipients, lactose, mannitol and trehalose were combined with varying concentrations of L-leucine (3% to 30% relative to the sugar or sugar alcohol) and trileucine (3%) as dispersion enhancers. The goal was to address key formulation hurdles: maintaining siRNA gene-silencing efficiency, optimizing solid-state properties, and achieving efficient aerosolization for pulmonary delivery. Lactose and trehalose-based spray-dried powders exhibited yields over 70% and preserved siRNA bioactivity, with gene silencing efficiencies exceeding 95% in vitro. Physicochemical characterization revealed that these formulations containing low to moderate leucine or trileucine content solidified in the glassy state, displaying glass transition temperatures over 76 °C and residual moisture levels below 7%, favorable for long-term stability and pulmonary delivery. In contrast, mannitol-based formulations were highly crystalline and less compatible with LNPs, resulting in low yields, larger, irregular shaped particles and poor aerosolization efficiency. In vitro aerosol performance was assessed using two breath-actuated DPIs in a laser diffraction inhalation setup. Our findings highlight that successful pulmonary delivery of siRNA-LNP powders not only depend on powder attributes but also on the interplay between formulation and DPI device. Optimizing excipient selection with regard to a device's powder dispersion principle is essential to achieve robust aerosol performance, efficient lung deposition, and preservation of therapeutic activity in solid-state siRNA-LNP dry powder formulations.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) generally responds to the ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) alectinib; however, some patients experience rapid disease progression shortly after treatment initiation. This study investigated the molecular features underlying this clinically distinct phenotype and evaluated potential therapeutic strategies using patient-derived models. METHODS: A 68-year-old woman with ALK-positive NSCLC experienced disease progression within 1 month of first-line alectinib therapy despite an initial transient tumor response. Two resistant cell lines were established from an adrenal metastasis and a pleural effusion, respectively. Histopathological and molecular characterization was performed. The combination of ALK-TKIs and the B-cell lymphoma 2 family inhibitor navitoclax was evaluated in vitro and in vivo. RESULTS: Both cell lines harbored the EML4-ALK fusion variant 1 without secondary ALK mutations and demonstrated resistance to multiple ALK-TKIs. Transcriptomic profiling demonstrated epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated features in the resistant cell lines, supported by concordant immunohistochemical findings in the pretreatment specimen. Melanoma-associated antigen 3 (MAGE-A3) was identified as the most highly upregulated gene, and its knockdown significantly enhanced ALK-TKI sensitivity. Navitoclax combined with ALK-TKIs synergistically reduced cell viability and enhanced apoptosis in vitro, and lorlatinib plus navitoclax produced greater antitumor efficacy than either monotherapy in vivo. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that pre-existing EMT-associated features, together with MAGE-A3 upregulation and impaired apoptotic signaling, may contribute to rapid disease progression during alectinib treatment in a subset of ALK-positive NSCLC patients. Targeting apoptotic vulnerability with navitoclax in combination with ALK-TKIs warrants further investigation as a therapeutic strategy for this resistance phenotype.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have become an important component of systemic therapy for esophageal cancer, but real-world safety data for combining ICIs with taxane- and platinum-based chemotherapy remain limited. This study compared adverse-event (AE) profiles, time to onset (TTO), and reported mortality between ICI-based combination therapy and ICI monotherapy in esophageal cancer. METHODS: Using the FDA adverse event reporting system (FAERS), we screened reports from Q3/2019 through Q1/2026 for esophageal cancer involving pembrolizumab or nivolumab as the primary suspect. Combination included immunotherapy with a taxane and platinum; monotherapy included immunotherapy alone. Disproportionality was assessed via reporting odds ratios (RORs) and proportional reporting ratios (PRRs). TTO was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox models, and logistic regression examined factors for reported mortality. RESULTS: Among 1,580 eligible reports (103 combination, 1,477 monotherapy), distinct AE signal profiles emerged. In combination, prominent signals were gastrointestinal, hematologic, and respiratory, with esophagitis showing the strongest signal (ROR, 61.97; 95%CI, 22.80-168.48), followed by decreased lymphocyte count (ROR, 59.68; 95%CI, 28.99-122.83) and behaviour disorder (ROR, 42.85; 95%CI, 13.58-135.17). In monotherapy, signals were more immune-mediated, including immune-mediated cystitis (ROR, 261.05; 95%CI, 113.92-598.18), immune-mediated cholangitis (ROR, 87.65; 95%CI, 41.36-185.78), immune-mediated endocrinopathy (ROR, 85.51; 95%CI, 27.19-268.89) and so on. Among 571 reports with TTO data, AEs occurred significantly earlier in combination than monotherapy, with median TTOs of 23 days (IQR, 8-72) vs. 49 days (IQR, 21-129) (log-rank P < 0.001), consistent across age, sex, weight, and reporting-year subgroups. Reported mortality was 6.8% for combination vs. 21.1% for monotherapy. After multivariable adjustment, combination was associated with lower reported mortality odds than monotherapy (adjusted OR, 0.27; 95%CI, 0.06-0.77; P = 0.033). CONCLUSION: ICI-based combination therapy showed a distinct AE profile and significantly earlier AE onset than monotherapy, but lower reported mortality odds. These findings underscore the need for early monitoring of hematologic, gastrointestinal, and respiratory toxicities during combination therapy.
